function: Probabilistic device scheduling (which UAVs upload gradients) for AirComp-enabled FL, with energy virtual queues; no physical-layer aggregation design is optimized or learned (pp. 1, 7).
notes: Excluded under above_phy, after codes 1 to 3 did not apply: research article, not a survey, and FL over the air passes the learning check. The contribution is a scheduling mechanism: "energy-conscious device scheduling mechanism" (p. 1). The only decision variables are the scheduling probabilities ("the device scheduling problem is formulated as", p. 7, with Theorem 2 on p. 7). The AirComp uplink uses a given channel-inversion rule (p. 5) and the power scaling factor is a fixed simulation constant of 0.001 (Table III, p. 8), so no aggregation, transceiver or RIS design is made. The comparison is against four scheduling heuristics ("we adopt four state-of-the-art baselines namely", p. 9). The function code would also apply. Borderline for the reviewer: if scheduling for AirComp FL is accepted as area 7, the facts are no RIS, a custom LoS channel at 2 GHz with unit fading (pp. 5, 9), MNIST and CIFAR-10 (p. 9), complexity O(log(1/eps)+|S_t|) (p. 8), no code link, and baselines that the paper itself modified into probabilistic form (p. 9, footnote 6).
